author: Thomas à Kempis
title: Of the intimate love of Jesus

verses.text: When Jesus is present all is well and nothing seemeth hard, but when Jesus is not present everything is hard.
verses.modernizedText: When Jesus is present all is well and nothing seems hard, but when Jesus is not present everything is hard.

verses.text: When Jesus speaketh not within, our comfort is nothing worth, but if Jesus speaketh but a single word great is the comfort we experience.
verses.modernizedText: When Jesus does not speak within, our comfort is worth nothing, but if Jesus speaks only a single word, great is the comfort we experience.

verses.text: Did not Mary Magdalene rise up quickly from the place where she wept when Martha said to her, The Master is come and calleth for thee?(1) Happy hour when Jesus calleth thee from tears to the joy of the spirit!
verses.modernizedText: Did not Mary Magdalene rise quickly from the place where she wept when Martha said to her, The Master has come and calls for you?(1) Happy hour when Jesus calls you from tears to the joy of the spirit!

verses.text: How dry and hard art thou without Jesus!
verses.modernizedText: How dry and hard you are without Jesus!

verses.text: How senseless and vain if thou desirest aught beyond Jesus!
verses.modernizedText: How senseless and vain if you desire anything beyond Jesus!

verses.text: Is not this greater loss than if thou shouldst lose the whole world?
verses.modernizedText: Is this not a greater loss than if you lost the whole world?

verses.text: What can the world profit thee without Jesus?
verses.modernizedText: What good can the world do you without Jesus?

verses.text: To be without Jesus is the nethermost hell, and to be with Jesus is sweet paradise.
verses.modernizedText: To be without Jesus is the lowest hell, and to be with Jesus is sweet paradise.

verses.text: If Jesus were with thee no enemy could hurt thee.
verses.modernizedText: If Jesus were with you, no enemy could hurt you.

verses.text: He who findeth Jesus findeth a good treasure, yea, good above all good; and he who loseth Jesus loseth exceeding much, yea, more than the whole world.
verses.modernizedText: The person who finds Jesus finds a good treasure, indeed, good above all good; and the person who loses Jesus loses exceedingly much, indeed, more than the whole world.

verses.text: Most poor is he who liveth without Jesus, and most rich is he who is much with Jesus.
verses.modernizedText: Most poor is the person who lives without Jesus, and most rich is the person who is much with Jesus.

verses.text: It is great skill to know how to live with Jesus, and to know how to hold Jesus is great wisdom.
verses.modernizedText: It is great skill to know how to live with Jesus, and great wisdom to know how to hold Jesus.

verses.text: Be thou humble and peaceable and Jesus shall be with thee.
verses.modernizedText: Be humble and peaceable, and Jesus will be with you.

verses.text: Be godly and quiet, and Jesus will remain with thee.
verses.modernizedText: Be godly and quiet, and Jesus will remain with you.

verses.text: Thou canst quickly drive away Jesus and lose His favour if thou wilt turn away to the outer things.
verses.modernizedText: You can quickly drive Jesus away and lose His favor if you turn away to outward things.

verses.text: And if thou hast put Him to flight and lost Him, to whom wilt thou flee, and whom then wilt thou seek for a friend?
verses.modernizedText: And if you have put Him to flight and lost Him, to whom will you flee, and whom will you then seek as a friend?

verses.text: Without a friend thou canst not live long, and if Jesus be not thy friend above all thou shalt be very sad and desolate.
verses.modernizedText: Without a friend you cannot live long, and if Jesus is not your friend above all, you will be very sad and desolate.

verses.text: Madly therefore doest thou if thou trusteth or findest joy in any other.
verses.modernizedText: Therefore, you act madly if you trust or find joy in any other.

verses.text: It is preferable to have the whole world against thee, than Jesus offended with thee.
verses.modernizedText: It is preferable to have the whole world against you than to have Jesus offended with you.

verses.text: Therefore of all that are dear to thee, let Jesus be specially loved.
verses.modernizedText: Therefore, of all who are dear to you, let Jesus be especially loved.

verses.text: Let all be loved for Jesus’ sake, but Jesus for His own.
verses.modernizedText: Let all be loved for Jesus’ sake, but Jesus for His own.

verses.text: Jesus Christ alone is to be specially loved, for He alone is found good and faithful above all friends.
verses.modernizedText: Jesus Christ alone is to be especially loved, for He alone is found good and faithful above all friends.

verses.text: For His sake and in Him let both enemies and friends be dear to thee, and pray for them all that they may all know and love Him.
verses.modernizedText: For His sake and in Him let both enemies and friends be dear to you, and pray for them all that they may all know and love Him.

verses.text: Never desire to be specially praised or loved, because this belongeth to God alone, who hath none like unto Himself.
verses.modernizedText: Never desire to be especially praised or loved, because this belongs to God alone, who has none like Himself.

verses.text: Nor wish thou that any one set his heart on thee, nor do thou give thyself up to the love of any, but let Jesus be in thee and in every good man.
verses.modernizedText: Do not wish anyone to set his heart on you, nor give yourself up to the love of anyone, but let Jesus be in you and in every good person.

verses.text: Be pure and free within thyself, and be not entangled by any created thing.
verses.modernizedText: Be pure and free within yourself, and do not be entangled by any created thing.

verses.text: Thou oughtest to bring a bare and clean heart to God, if thou desirest to be ready to see how gracious the Lord is.
verses.modernizedText: You ought to bring a bare and clean heart to God if you desire to be ready to see how gracious the Lord is.

verses.text: And in truth, unless thou be prevented and drawn on by His grace, thou wilt not attain to this, that having cast out and dismissed all else, thou alone art united to God.
verses.modernizedText: And in truth, unless you are anticipated and drawn on by His grace, you will not attain this: that having cast out and dismissed all else, you alone are united to God.

verses.text: For when the grace of God cometh to a man, then he becometh able to do all things, and when it departeth then he will be poor and weak and given up unto troubles.
verses.modernizedText: For when the grace of God comes to a person, he becomes able to do all things, and when it departs he will be poor and weak and given up to troubles.

verses.text: In these thou art not to be cast down nor to despair, but to rest with calm mind on the will of God, and to bear all things which come upon thee unto the praise of Jesus Christ; for after winter cometh summer, after night returneth day, after the tempest a great calm.
verses.modernizedText: In these you must not be cast down or despair, but rest with a calm mind on the will of God and bear all things that come upon you to the praise of Jesus Christ; for after winter comes summer, after night returns day, after the tempest a great calm.
